findings.reason: the section would add a second ctest reader and a test proving behaviour the shared reader already has; the honest change is to find why the promotion-side caller did not reach this reader (or was given a log whose header lacked the colon), which is a different fix and a different gate.
findings.text: §37 asks that a ctest failure summary be read "alongside the pytest form read today", but `review.gate_log_failure_ids` already reads both: `_gate_log_format` (reckon/crew/review.py:2916) returns `"ctest"` whenever `_CTEST_FAILED_HEADER_RE` (`^The following tests FAILED:\s*$`, reckon/crew/review.py:2314) or `_CTEST_SUMMARY_RE` (`tests failed out of`, reckon/crew/review.py:2328) appears, `_ctest_failure_ids` (reckon/crew/review.py:2770) then returns the block's entries, and `_CTEST_ENTRY_RE` (`^\s*\d+\s*-\s*(.+?)\s+\(([^)]*)\)\s*$`, reckon/crew/review.py:2315) already matches the exact entry the section quotes, `1155 - unit/imas/iron_limb_outline (Failed)`.

findings.reason: the fix is threading the run's real head revision through an existing carry path, not building a new tree; a node brief that does not name `_partition_runner`'s `head_sha` will rebuild the carry and leave the control arm broken.
findings.text: §30 says the control-mutation measure "builds its own tree and still asks a revision for a file that revision does not hold", but both halves of the mechanism already exist: `_carry_missing_tests` (reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:590) copies the head's copy of a missing test into the base tree, and `_partition_runner` composes the same carry into each job's script (`carry`, reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:957-962, `git archive {head_sha} -- {path}`). The actual defect is one argument: `control_mutation_observation` calls `_partition_runner` with `head_sha=base_sha` (reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:1442-1452), so the carry archives the file from the base revision that does not hold it and `set -euo pipefail` aborts the script — which is exactly the `fatal: pathspec` plus `tar: This does not look like a tar archive` the section quotes.

findings.reason: the section must extend the one reader so both the `suite run` path and the promotion path read a prose status identically, and name that the refusal is the existing one, not a parallel parse.
findings.text: §31 asks that "a gate exit status that opens with an integer is read as that integer", but one reader already owns that question: `_gate_exit_status` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3504) reads `report.exit_status` then `result.exit_status` and does `int(value)`, returning `None` for `"0 (job 1335599, all_debug, …)"` because `int` of the trailing prose raises. It is the same reader the caller at reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2358 and :5312 closes the gate with. A second parser in the acceptance path (reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:707 refuses "the run records no passing gate") would read the same field two ways.

findings.reason: the refusal must sit in the manifest reader that already owns duplicate-key detection, so every reader (classification, promotion, audit) sees the same refusal and one implementation covers both the same-line and separate-line forms.
findings.text: §36 asks that a manifest with two `tests:` lines be refused before any gate runs, quoting each line, but the manifest reader already refuses a duplicated field: `_two_keys_on_one_line_message` (reckon/crew/reports.py:288) names the path and line and explains that reading both "would turn the earlier value into a corrupted string and the later key into an empty list". §36's case is the sibling defect — two `tests:` lines on separate lines — and the owner is the same reader, whose `_MANIFEST_KEY_ALTERNATION` already knows the key. A check added in the promotion path would leave the manifest reader accepting a record promotion refuses.

findings.reason: the sections must extend the existing release path (and make its pointer compare read the file twice rather than compare a stale copy), not add a command that bypasses it; the census of the defect is both compares at :91 and :1255.
findings.text: §34's defect is the compare `if dict(current) != pointer: refusal = "the live pointer changed before workspace release"` (reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:1255, and its twin at :91), which compares the caller's own copy against the file rather than the file against the file. The section asks for "one command" to retire a landed head, but the retirement path already exists in `promotion_release.py` (`_release_after_promotion`, called from reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:1266) and the landed-head release in `_release_measurement_worktree` (reckon/crew/pending_landing.py:1230). A second one-step command beside them would be a second owner of retirement.

findings.reason: eight sections adding to a 25-family surface without an account of what they replace is exactly the accretion the budget rule exists to stop; at minimum §31 and §36 replace mechanisms already named above and should be recorded as such.
findings.text: §30 adds a refusal ("a measure that cannot build its tree is refused naming the path and the revision it asked") to the refusal_families 25 family, §31 adds "refused naming the field and the revision it asked", §32 adds "promoted … records that the manifest was unreadable", §33 adds one obligation quoting two texts, §34 adds "a release that is refused says which field differed", §35 adds a second condition to repair-resume refusal, §36 adds "refused before any gate runs, quoting each line", and §37 adds a red/green verdict for a second log format; not one of the eight names a refusal it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be.

findings.reason: the section must state which existing recovery class an unrecognised status maps to and extend `recovery_classification`/`recovery_vocabulary` (and `_wait_probe_shape_refusal` for the probe), otherwise the run is classified twice and the two verdicts can disagree.
findings.text: §33's endpoint — a run whose manifest status is outside the recognised set is classed as needing its coordinator rather than complete — is the verdict the one classifier already produces: `manifest_status_is_template` (reckon/crew/reports.py:145) and the reader comment at reckon/crew/reports.py:126 ("unrecognised spelling is not proof of work") already define the vocabulary, `RECOVERY_CLASSES` (reckon/crew/recovery_vocabulary.py:33) already carries `unreadable`, `exited-unfinished` and `stopped` as the distinct outcomes for such a record, and `_wait_probe_shape_refusal` (reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py:462) already refuses a probe that "is a scalar rather than a list" — the prose `wait_probe` the section describes. A new classifier or a new obligation family would be a second classifier over the same fields.
